full_prompt:
Draw exactly ONE Small Seal glyph U+3D063.
The supplied chart shows FOUR historical views of the SAME ONE Small Seal character, ordered THX, CCZ, QJZ, DYC. Compare EVERY available witness equally; any slot marked unavailable provides no evidence. Create ONE newly drawn, coherent contemporary sans-serif/Gothic glyph informed by all witnesses, selecting ONE coherent attested construction where variants differ. Never combine incompatible components or replace this with modern Chinese. Trace the real continuous writing-stroke courses using smooth rounded curves and appropriate straight segments; preserve all meaningful branches, legs, bars, counters, crossings, attachments and detachments. Each intentional stroke has the SAME CONSTANT width, approximately 3% of the full canvas, with rounded caps and joins. No brush taper, thick/thin pressure, serifs, texture, ink blobs, doubled outlines or ornamental seal effects. Output exactly ONE complete glyph, black on transparent alpha, centered within the central70% of a square canvas with generous clear margins. No reference copies, four-character layout, labels, text, frames, grid, backdrop or shadows.
STRUCTURAL READING AID:
1. THX, CCZ and QJZ available; DYC unavailable. Left ritual component has shorter detached upper horizontal and longer lower horizontal with attached long center descender and TWO detached side descenders.
2. Right component has exactly FIVE downward stroke ends: TWO short detached flanking side strokes and THREE longer central legs. The flanking strokes begin around upper-third height and end above the lowest legs.
3. Of the three long central legs: the left main tall stem begins high, descends then curves outward LEFT to its lower end; from its upper-third there is a short RIGHTWARD bridge which bends downward into the MIDDLE long vertical leg. That bridge and middle leg connect to the left main stem.
4. The other main tall stem begins slightly higher on the right and descends separately, curving gently outward RIGHT at bottom. It is detached from the left main stem and middle leg. TWO high main stem starts plus TWO lower flanking starts; middle long leg begins from bridge, not from a fifth upper tip.
5. No rings/counters or enclosing box; no extra horizontal crossing bars. Preserve the short bridge, its correct attachment, five separate bottom ends and the relative shortness of both flanking strokes.
Count carefully: THREE left ritual descenders plus FIVE right descending ends, eight lower ends overall. Use real continuous rounded stem-to-leg curves. Keep the right main tall stroke independent; do not join all three central legs together.
